requirements.statement: A party picker's results sit under a heading asking the trader to select an address, with the count straight under it, eight a page counted against every address the picker found, whether the role's whole list or the matches when a search narrows it, and the design system's pagination follows the table where more than eight were found, its links carrying the search term and the address held as chosen. An inset above the results names whichever address the picker currently holds as chosen, between the search box and the results, on every page and after a search, the address coming from the address in the request, the posted field or the party's saved answer so the name shows on a page that does not hold its row. The results table is one fieldset whose visually hidden legend repeats the heading so a screen reader names the group of addresses, and with no matches the message takes the place of the count.
requirements.why: An organisation's address book grows past one screen, so the picker pages, and naming the chosen address above the results is what tells a trader on the second page what they have already chosen.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-311, repo-frontend-p19-314 and repo-frontend-p19-315, which the design record states as built; ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-022 pages the pickers at eight and ruling-ian-2026-11-23-p1-011 restores the restatement of the chosen address with the paging.

requirements.statement: The edit control on a section follows that section's address whether the picker copied it onto the notification or a fill-from control took it from the paired party, and with no address held the edit page sends the trader to the picker; reopening a party's picker pre-ticks the record that party's address was picked from while the role's list still holds it. A picker is reached from the consignment addresses page rather than the hub, so it ends with the primary control alone. A save with nothing chosen leaves without refusing and commits nothing, so the role stays empty or keeps the address it held; an address not in the book, or no longer in it, is refused with the role's own error; and a missing or deleted selection travels as no selection while the context a change link carried is kept on every way out of the picker.
requirements.why: A trader who opens a picker to look and leaves without choosing should not lose the address the notification already holds, and pre-ticking the record they picked from shows them where the address came from.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-309, repo-frontend-p19-310, repo-frontend-p19-312 and repo-frontend-p19-317.

requirements.statement: The permanent address section is a third section shape on the consignment addresses page, alongside the party sections and the county parish holding section, for a consignment carrying a cat, dog or ferret line, its hint being a lead-in sentence followed by two bullets rather than the party sections' single line. Once every animal needing one has a permanent address the section shows one address, every addressable animal being saved against the place of destination or only one animal needing one, and otherwise one line saying how many animals have an address added, counting the animals that need one. Either shape carries a control to change it and no edit control, because the address was hand-entered or copied from the place of destination on the permanent address page and never picked from the address book, so there is no record there to edit.
requirements.why: A hand-entered address has no address-book record behind it, so offering to edit that record would lead nowhere, and one line for many animals keeps the page readable.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-318 to repo-frontend-p19-320; which commodities the section applies to is the identification and permanent address area's to settle from the data dictionary.

requirements.statement: The county parish holding number page keeps its three part labels on screen, because three unlabelled boxes under one legend would be harder to use than the single field they replace, and the number being two digits of county, three of parish and four of holding, its example hint shows that grouping with no comma and no full stop; its help names the animal and plant health documents, then links to the guidance for checking a holding's details. The boxes set no character limit, so nothing typed or pasted is cut short: when the county box holds nine digits with or without spaces or slashes and the other two are empty the number is split into its three parts on save, and anything else goes through the per-part checks unchanged with every box keeping what was typed. Each box turns the browser's saved values off and asks for a digit keypad, nothing moves focus between the boxes, and one error message belongs to the group rather than to each box, the date-input row classes only sitting the boxes side by side. The page can be saved with every box empty: no number is saved, any number saved before is cleared, and the gap is held at submission rather than refused on the page. The number is stored as nine bare digits.
requirements.why: A trader copying a number off a document should be able to paste it whole, and holding the gap at submission lets them come back to the page without being blocked on it.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-321 to repo-frontend-p19-329; ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09-p1-013 has the boxes follow the date input with no script on top, which repo-frontend-p19-324 to repo-frontend-p19-326 record as built.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page is reached only from the permanent address section of the consignment addresses page, for a consignment carrying a cat, dog or ferret line, and its cards come from the animal identifier records already entered, one per animal, never from the line's animal count, because the address is stored on the identifier record so a card can only exist once that record does. When at least one line needs a permanent address and no line that needs one has an animal identified yet, the page shows no cards and a message takes their place: "Identify an animal on identification details before you can continue.", linking to the identification details page, when any such line carries a number of animals, and "Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue.", linking to the consignment details page, when none does. While the message shows, the save control still renders but writes nothing. Each card asks once, as its own radio group legend, whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, and the page carries no second question above the cards.
requirements.why: Driving the cards off the identifier records keeps the page from offering a card it cannot store an answer against, and asking once per card keeps the answer with the animal it belongs to.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-330, repo-frontend-p19-331, repo-frontend-p19-333 and repo-frontend-p19-452 to repo-frontend-p19-455; the permanent address feature's English copy holds both messages.

requirements.statement: Choosing to enter a new address on a permanent address card requires the name or organisation name, the first address line, the town or city, the postcode, an email address and a phone number, while the second address line and the county may be left blank, and every field's character limit and over-long message are the ones the owning address rules already build for the party edit page, the page stating only its own required messages and no format check on the email, the phone or the postcode. Choosing the place of destination before the notification has one is refused on that card's radio group, naming no animal on the field or in the summary, while an address field's refusal names the card's animal in the error summary and stays plain on the field itself. The new-address fields ask no country, a hand-entered address always recording the United Kingdom, and the phone field is the one field with a hint, because a trader giving an address outside the United Kingdom cannot otherwise know the number is dialled from here. An animal left with neither option chosen saves with no permanent address, the save still succeeding for the others.
requirements.why: Naming the animal in the summary is what lets a trader find the card that needs fixing on a page of many, and saving the cards that are answered keeps their work while they find the rest.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-334 to repo-frontend-p19-340.

requirements.statement: The documents file field is labelled as the attachment, the noun the review also uses, and the reference field has no hint. The status column reports the check's progress, scanning for a virus and the check being completed, and on a refusal names the reason the upload service gave where the page has wording for it, a virus found, the upload failing or the download failing, a reason it has no wording for staying as rejected rather than being named wrongly. A document is started by any of its reference, its type whether offered or not, its date of issue text or a chosen file, and any save control then keeps every answer typed, says what is missing and adds nothing, or adds the document when it is complete, rather than dropping the part-filled form; every field is mandatory per record and there is no edit page, so presence is checked when a document is added, and the error summary lists the fields in the order they appear on the page. The type list opens on its select text, which carries no value, so a form left on it submits an empty type, and one message covers both mistakes a list can make, being left on the select text or carrying a value the page never offered; the offered types are served by the service and primed at boot so the check is built for each add rather than frozen at module load, and the list's items, the add form's check and the vocabulary this service sends to the backend are one ordered list, so the order the page offers is the order that list states.
requirements.why: Keeping a part-filled document on the page rather than dropping it is what stops a trader re-typing a reference after a missed field, and one ordered list of types keeps the page, the check and the backend from disagreeing.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-341 to repo-frontend-p19-343 and repo-frontend-p19-357 to repo-frontend-p19-360.

requirements.statement: The documents file size limit is whatever the documents upload configuration holds and nothing else states a figure, the page states that same figure and checks it in the browser for any submit that sends the file, so a trader learns a file is too large before spending time uploading it, and the upload service decides for itself whether to take a file and may refuse one as too large on receipt, which the page renders in its own wording. While the add form is open every save control posts the form and its file to the upload service's own scanning session rather than to this service, that session being opened with the size limit to enforce so the ingress body cap does not bound it; when the form is closed, or a taken-on document or a removal is waiting to be retried, the save controls post to this service and send no file, so the retry runs before anything else on the page. A file carrying no bytes is the right type and under the size limit, so it reaches the page rather than being stopped before it, and the page is where it is refused and nothing is added. A document saved by adding another or by the save-and-return control is followed by a redirect so a reload cannot replay the save, while one saved by Save and continue is answered on the returned request by the save choice, a reload of that response saving nothing twice because a document already listed is not added again, and nothing holds the trader for a scan still running. A render reuses the upload session the page is already showing while that session is still waiting for its file, carried in the refresh link and a hidden field, so a scan being polled does not leave a run of registrations behind; a render carrying no handle, and one whose session has already taken its file, opens a session of its own, which keeps two concurrent adds off one handle, and the carried handle is looked up on the notification rather than trusted alone, so a handle another notification opened reaches nothing. A form carrying a session that has already taken its file is answered by the upload service and never by this one, because the save controls post the file straight there, the page being served with no store and the feature's client bundle opening it again by its own address when the browser hands back a copy it kept. The query key the trader returns under is the trader-facing word for what they return from and its value is the correlation handle, because no upload identifier exists when the session opens, and the return path is relative because the upload service refuses an absolute redirect outside development. A well-formed upload identifier from another journey is answered as not found rather than as forbidden, so the journey never confirms that upload exists.
requirements.why: Posting the file straight to the upload service is what lets a large attachment past the ingress body cap, and looking a carried handle up on the notification is what keeps one trader's upload session out of another's notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-344 to repo-frontend-p19-350 and repo-frontend-p19-361 to repo-frontend-p19-368.

requirements.statement: The documents page uses the full-width surface so the added-documents table fits, its guidance and its fields keeping a two-thirds reading width, and with no documents the upload card shows no table and no sentence. The reference cell breaks a long unbroken reference onto further lines so the table stays inside the card, and each row's actions sit at its right-hand end. The reason the add control is shut sits before the control it refuses, and the control keeps its place in the tab order so the error summary can reach it; the limit error links to the documents already added rather than to the attachment field, because at the cap the add control is shut and pointing a trader at the file input would send them to a control they cannot use, while the table shows the documents they already hold. The drop zone's wording matches the design system's own defaults. A document's file is opened with a link rather than a submit so it needs no token, and a file is offered only once its scan has settled clean. The status tag carries a visually hidden name for the document it belongs to, so a screen reader hears what was checked. With JavaScript on, the upload control the page shows is not the original file input, so the oversize summary error points at the control a trader can focus rather than at the hidden input behind it.
requirements.why: Pointing an error at a control the trader can actually focus is what makes the error summary usable, and offering a file only once its scan is clean keeps an unchecked file from being opened.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-351 to repo-frontend-p19-356 and repo-frontend-p19-367 to repo-frontend-p19-372.

requirements.statement: A document the scan rejected holds the continue back, as does a document the upload service has taken on that the notification does not list, because otherwise the trader would carry on with a claimed document missing from the notification, while the exit to the overview waits for neither.
requirements.why: A trader must not reach the declaration believing a document is attached when the notification does not hold it, and a trader who only wants to stop should not be held by a scan.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-362.

requirements.statement: A trader's own uploaded document is served under a cache policy a decision has settled, saying what a shared or browser cache may keep of it.
requirements.why: The goal is the look and feel of the notification journey, and no source in this programme settles what a cache may keep of a trader's document: the design record carries it as still to be settled, with the page served with no store because a kept copy of it can post to a spent upload session, so the open decision is reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: The design record states that a document's file is served with no cache directive of its own and records what a cache may keep of a trader's own document as still to be settled (repo-frontend-p19-371).

requirements.statement: The arrival date's hint gives a fixed date showing the format rather than a date tied to the arrival window, the date widget's bounds and the out-of-range message policing the window, and the arrival details page reads the window once per request and hands it to both the widget and the checks, so the two cannot disagree across midnight, a reading with no widget taking the window as it stands.
requirements.why: A hint that moved with the window would read as part of the rule, and reading the window once is what keeps the widget and the refusal from disagreeing at midnight.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-373 and repo-frontend-p19-374.

requirements.statement: The port search shows a placeholder asking the trader to select a port in its empty box, in the same words as the select text that is the first entry of the list shown without JavaScript. The means of transport options read air, rail, road and sea, and each stores its own reference code. The transport identification hint is a lead-in and one bullet per alternative, so the number of choices shows at a glance.
requirements.why: Using one wording in the box and in the list keeps the question the same on both paths, and one bullet per alternative shows a trader at a glance what they may give.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-375 to repo-frontend-p19-377.

requirements.statement: A transit country is added to the table when the trader presses the add control, and removing one submits the page's form so the token travels with it and no load can trigger it, the country's code riding in the button's value so the row pressed is the row removed however the list has been reordered since the page rendered. The status message region ships empty and the page's script writes the message into it just after load, because a live region already holding its text when the document is parsed is read as ordinary page content, both adding and removing being full form submits so the message arrives with a fresh document every time. The added-countries list names each country rather than its code, because the list is the whole record of the answer the trader reads back, and the cap is not stated up front: the search goes when the last country is added and the status message says why. The page's browser title is the short task name rather than its question heading, the search's select text asks for a choice while its empty-box text asks for a search, because the two do different things, and a country already added stays in the list and a repeat is refused by name, which tells the trader more than a country quietly missing from the list. The page offers the same countries and territories as the country of origin page, each territory named with its country, rather than every code the label lookup resolves. An empty list is a valid answer because the question is optional, while a list holding a country not offered is refused, on submit as not from the list and on a stored answer as no longer available, and a stored list is checked against the page's rules when it opens, a banner naming any country no longer offered before the continue saves the filtered list. The page names the choice once, a heading above the search box and the table with the fieldset round the table carrying the same words visually hidden, so a screen-reader user hears the group named and a sighted user reads the words once.
requirements.why: The table is itself the confirmation that a country was added or removed, and refusing a repeat by name tells a trader why their choice did not appear instead of leaving them guessing.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-378 to repo-frontend-p19-390; ruling-design-2026-11-13-p1-003 keeps the add control and ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-008 makes the table its own confirmation, both of which the record states as built.

requirements.statement: The transporter list shows its facts in headed columns with a status tag, green for an approved transporter and magenta for a newly added one, and a transporter with no approval number reads as not applicable in that column. Searching the list filters it in place: nothing is checked or committed, and a picked row stays picked when the search leaves it on the list. With JavaScript the list narrows in the page as the trader types, because the page already holds the whole list and needs no endpoint, the matching letters in each shown cell being bold and a polite live region saying how many rows are shown, and pressing the search control or Enter runs the same filter and posts nothing, so the page keeps the whole list to filter again; without JavaScript the search is a submit on the page's own form and the server returns the narrowed list, the pick travelling through a search in a hidden field and the search and the save being told apart by the value of the control pressed. A transporter picked and then filtered out of view stays picked, the filter hiding rows and never clearing a choice. The search matches the name, the address, the approval number, the type and the status, ignoring case and accents, so a trader typing plain letters finds an accented name, and a transporter with no approval number is matched by the words its column shows; a term running across two cells, such as an address into an approval number, still finds its row, and because no single cell holds the whole term nothing is bold. The control to add a transporter sits on the search row, right-aligned above the table, dropping below the search on a phone, and the tab order is the search box, the search control, the add control, then the rows.
requirements.why: Filtering a list the page already holds keeps a trader's choice while they look for another, and matching across cells is what finds a row when a trader pastes something spanning two columns.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-391 to repo-frontend-p19-397, with the in-place filter at repo-frontend-p19-381. Where transporter records are held is the transporter area's to settle.

requirements.statement: The transporter type question warns the trader to check the transporter list before adding a new transporter, so they do not add a duplicate, offers private first with no hint and commercial with an explanation of the Northern Ireland condition, and its one control is a continue rather than a save. Each add form opens only for the type it belongs to, opening or posting it for any other stored type, or none, returning the trader to the type question. A commercial transporter added by hand can only be from Northern Ireland, so its country is shown rather than asked and a posted value naming anywhere else has been tampered with and is refused, and the commercial form opens with the authorisation rules the transporter list states, read from the list's own copy. Both forms close the address at the country, then head the contact details with the email before the phone, and both hint the international dialling code. A transporter typed in by hand joins the organisation's list as new rather than approved, and a private transporter's country is held as both the display name and its code, so neither storing it nor reading it back needs a lookup.
requirements.why: Warning the trader before they add is cheaper than de-duplicating a list afterwards, and showing a country that can only be one value saves a question that has one answer.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-398 to repo-frontend-p19-405; ruling-ian-2026-11-06-p1-038 forces a commercial transporter's country with no reference-data lookup, which repo-frontend-p19-401 records as built. How that country is stored, and where a transporter record lives, are the transporter area's to settle against the service.

requirements.statement: The link that adds a transporter carries where the trader came from, and the add form's own save carries it on to the transporter list, so a trader sent from check your answers goes on from the list like any other start. Saving a complete record on either add form returns the trader to the list with the saved transporter as the first row, already chosen, under a one-time success banner titled for success and reading the transporter's name with only its first letter capitalised followed by the words that a transporter was added, the banner showing on that one view only and a reload or a later return showing the list with no banner. Values entered on a form whose save was refused are shown again in its fields the next time the trader opens that form, until the form is saved or cancelled, while the secondary control on each form discards them, commits nothing to the notification and takes the trader to the dashboard, wherever the notification list lives. The transporter type question and the private add form carry no status strip, while the list and the commercial add form do. Where the stored type was not changed on the way into an add form, the transporter chosen before the add began is still chosen after cancelling, and a trader who changed the type at the type question on the way in is left with the type they chose and no transporter, the type question's own purge having removed the other type's stored transporter before the add form opened.
requirements.why: Showing the saved transporter first and already chosen is what saves the trader finding it again, and keeping refused values until the form is saved or cancelled is what stops them re-typing an address.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-406 to repo-frontend-p19-410, with the trail carried at repo-frontend-p19-382 and the status strip at repo-frontend-p19-400.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's own code-quality rules bind every change to it: a comment describes only the lines below it and only where a name or an extraction cannot, making no claim about callers, other modules, the backend, a library or a test and carrying no counts; no ticket key, backlog or ruling identifier, release name or session word appears in code, comments or test titles; no history is kept in code, so there is no before-and-after narration, no removed constants and no note of a rename; a name predicts what the code returns and changes, with no positional boolean flags, no metaphors and one name per concept, a rename covering the whole vocabulary; and set-up used by two tests lives in the shared helper, promoting a helper deleting the local copies. The lint script enforces the identifier, silent-catch, error-log and platform-layer rules through the repository's own lint rule module, and the identifier rule in template comments through a second one, and the canonical text of the rules lives in the workspace rather than in the repository.
requirements.why: Lint refusing a ticket key or a ruling identifier in code is what keeps a programme's own vocabulary out of the service, and one canonical text keeps every repository answering to the same rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-411 to repo-frontend-p19-416 and repo-frontend-p19-419: the repository records the rules and names the lint that enforces them.

requirements.statement: Every branch that changes an outcome logs once through the request's logger with the identifiers support searches by, logging the error object rather than only a message, and no request or response body is logged at information level. A test's title states what its assertions prove, and the test fails without the change it covers.
requirements.why: One log line per outcome with the identifiers support searches by is what makes a trader's report traceable, and a test that passes without its change proves nothing.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-417 and repo-frontend-p19-418.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend requires at least Node 26.13.1 and npm 11.6.2, the floor set in its engines field. It keeps its session in a Redis-backed cache when deployed and in memory for local development, which the cache engine setting overrides, the in-memory cache being unsuitable for production because it is neither shared between instances nor kept across a restart, while every deployed instance of a service shares one Redis store and a frontend may use only the keys prefixed with its own service name. Its Redis client pins the RESP2 wire protocol, because the client library defaults to RESP3 and the session store talks RESP2 to the managed Redis service. A forward proxy is set up by default and calls made with the platform fetch use the proxy dispatcher, a client that uses another HTTP library providing the dispatcher itself.
requirements.why: A session that is not shared between instances loses a trader's work on a deploy, a client speaking a protocol the store does not answer breaks every session, and a call that misses the proxy dispatcher fails only once it is deployed.

requirements.statement: For every page request it handles, the animals frontend counts the calls that request made to its journey backend, the times it read the signed-in session record from the session store, and every call it made to an HTTP dependency, by dependency and operation, the journey backend included, commands sent to the session store not counting as dependency calls. A page request is every request except the health check, the site icon, the static asset route and the counts endpoint itself, so a form post, a redirect, a rendered page, the not-found page and the document scan poll all count; a backend call is one call to the journey backend through the shared fetch helper, counted once even when a refused or slow connection is retried, and a session resolution is one read of the session record by the authentication plugin or by the view context, the session state the session library loads not being counted. A request's counts live in a per-request async store, the counts plugin running each request's lifecycle methods inside it because the server framework offers no public hook that runs a whole request in one async context, and because a view renders outside that context a session resolution is counted against the request it is read for rather than through the store. Running totals are kept per route and served from a counts endpoint, which a delete clears, answering with the service name, the time counting began, the totals and a list per route by method and path, each holding page requests, backend calls, session resolutions and external calls, the last keyed by dependency and then by operation; the performance suite reads them and reports the ratios. The endpoint is on by default for local development and off when deployed, and needs no sign-in, while the metrics are off locally and on when deployed, writing one metric document per page request carrying the backend calls and session resolutions marked as a page request.
requirements.why: Counting a request's backend and session reads is what shows a page that has quietly started making one call per row, and the performance suite's ratios are read from those counts.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's pre-commit hook is cheap, running the staged-file formatter and lint auto-fix on the staged files only, with no build and no tests, so a fix lands in the commit that caused it, while the pre-push hook is the full gate, running the format check, lint and the unit suite, which builds the frontend first. The slow half of the gate sits on the push rather than the commit because the suite is thousands of tests with coverage on top of a production build, mostly fixed startup cost that does not shrink for a small change, and charging that to every commit is what teaches people to skip the hooks, which skips the cheap format and lint checks as well, while a push is the first point the work affects anyone else. Installing dependencies installs both hooks. The whole gate, or just its fast half, can be run by hand at any time, and when the workspace's quality gate has already run the format check, lint and the suite for the exact commit and left a marker naming the verified revision, the pre-push hook skips rather than repeating it, while without that workspace the full gate always runs locally; the workspace gate runs its cheap checks before the build, so a formatting slip fails in seconds instead of after a full suite. The SonarCloud analysis the gate uploads is set up in the repo's own Sonar project properties file.
requirements.why: A cheap commit and a thorough push is what keeps people using the hooks instead of skipping them, and the shared marker stops the same suite running twice for one revision.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-429 to repo-frontend-p19-432 and the three notes beside them, with the SonarCloud set-up at repo-frontend-p19-437-m1.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend builds a development image and a production image from its Dockerfile, each run with the container's port 3000 published on the host's port 3000. The recommended path for local cross-service development is the workspace Docker stack, held in the trade imports workspace repository, which stands the identity stub up alongside the frontend with the right environment wiring and needs no host-file edits, while a standalone run against that stub needs its own environment file naming the sign-in configuration address, client identifier, client secret, service identifier and policy; the full local environment, the database, the file store, Redis, the stubs and every animals service including this one, is that stack, which can also be started built from local source or with this service left out to run natively. The session cookie's same-site setting is fixed at strict in the authentication plugin while the identity state cookie is lax by default and set by its own variable, because the identity callback is a cross-site top-level navigation on which a strict state cookie is not sent, so sign-in fails.
requirements.why: A strict state cookie silently breaks sign-in, so the reason it is lax has to be recorded beside the setting, and naming the stack as the local path saves each developer wiring the stubs by hand.
